name: France: South France
court: FRANCE - SOUTH FRANCE *CERTIFIED SOMMELIER EXAM ONLY*

outcome.certified: After studying this section, a candidate will be able to match regions in the South of France with their grape varieties and styles of wine made.

rows.certified: Provence: French Mediterranean coastline; From the border of Italy to the Rhône River.; Languedoc-Roussillon: Encompasses the entire southern coast of France, from the border of Italy along the Mediterranean coast line to the border with Spain.; Languedoc; Roussillon; Southwest France: South of Bordeaux and North of the Languedoc; Spanish Pyrenees border; Dordogne: Southeast of Bordeaux’s Right Bank; The Dordogne River; Flows west from its origin in the Massif Central, runs through the region of Bergerac.
Provence: Mediterranean; Languedoc-Roussillon: Mediterranean; Southwest France: Continental; Dordogne: Continental

Provence: Mediterranean Sea, rolling foothills; Languedoc-Roussillon: Rolling hillsides, steep cliffs, Mediterranean Sea; Southwest France: Pyrenees Mountains to the south, landlocked; Dordogne: Dordogne River
Languedoc-Roussillon: Large amount of IGP wines.; Pays d'Oc IGP

Provence: Nearly 90% dry rosé production.; Languedoc-Roussillon: Red, white, rosé, sweet wines, sparkling wines; Vins doux naturels are made by the process of mutage, a wine-making technique for making sweet wines where fermentation is stopped by the addition of neutral grape spirit.

Provence: Clairette, Ugni Blanc (Trebbiano in Italy), Rolle (Vermentino in Italy); Languedoc-Roussillon: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Clairette, Viognier, Muscat, Mauzac, Chenin Blanc; Southwest France: Petit Manseng, Gros Manseng
Provence: Grenache, Cinsault, Syrah, Mourvèdre; Languedoc-Roussillon: Grenache, Syrah, Carignan, Mourvèdre, and Cinsault; Southwest France: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cot (Malbec), Tannat

Provence: Côtes de Provence AOP; Grape Varieties: Cinsault, Grenache, Mourvèdre, Syrah; Wine Style: Dry rosé-dominant; Bandol AOP; Grape Varieties: Mourvèdre (min 50%), Grenache, Cinsault; Wine Style: Dry, red wine-dominant; Languedoc-Roussillon: LANGUEDOC; Limoux AOP; White Wines; Grape Varieties: Mauzac, Chenin Blanc, Chardonnay; Wine Style: Dry white wines; Red Wines; Grape Varieties: Merlot-dominant; Wine Style: Dry red wines; Crémant de Limoux AOP; Grape Varieties: Chardonnay, Chenin Blanc, Mauzac, Pinot Noir; Wine Style: Traditional method white and rosé sparkling wine.; Fitou AOP; Grape Varieties: Grenache, Carignan, Syrah, Mourvèdre; Wine Style: Dry red wines; Banyuls AOP/Banyuls Grand Cru AOP; Grape Varieties: Grenache; Wine Style: Vins Doux Naturels; Muscat de Rivesaltes AOP; Grape Varieties: Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains, Muscat of Alexandria; Wine Style: Vins Doux Naturels; Southwest France: Cahors AOP; Grape Varieties: Cot (Malbec)-dominant, additionally Merlot and Tannat; Wine Style: Dry red wines only; Madiran AOP; Grape Varieties: Tannat-dominant, additionally Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon; Wine Style: Dry red wines only; Jurançon AOP; Grape Varieties: Gros Manseng and Petit Manseng; Wine Style: White wines; Blanc Sec: Dry white wines; Blanc: Off-dry white wines; Dordogne: Bergerac AOP; Dordogne River; White Wine; Grape Varieties: Sémillon, Sauvignon Blanc, Sauvignon Gris, Muscadelle; Wine Style: Dry white wines; Red and Rosé Wine; Grape Varieties: Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Cot (Malbec), Merlot; Wine Style: Dry red and rosé; Monbazillac AOP; Dordogne River; White Wine; Grape Varieties: Muscadelle, Sauvignon Blanc, Sémillon; Wine Style: Botrytis-affected sweet wines
Provence: Bandol: Domaine Tempier, Château de Pibarnon, Château Pradeaux; Languedoc-Roussillon: Banyuls: Chapoutier, Domaine du Mas Blanc
Provence: Birthplace of wine in France. Has been producing wine since 600 BCE.; Southwest France: Has been growing grapes since 125 BC.

Provence: Dry rosé: Shellfish, fish, local fare, bouillabaisse.; Bandol: Beef, lamb; Languedoc-Roussillon: Banyuls:; Sweet: chocolate, nuts, coffee, creamy desserts, figs, prunes, dried fruit desserts.; Savory: Warm foie gras and figs, savory dishes with elements of sweetness, with fruit or in a sauce.; Salty blue cheeses; Southwest France: Cahors and Madiran:; Duck breast, rack of lamb, Foie Gras, cassoulet, dishes featuring Périgord truffles.; Dordogne: Monbazillac:; Sweet: Fruit-based desserts, peaches, caramel, citrus, apricots, pears, apple-based desserts.; Savory: Foie gras, savory dishes with sweeter sauces.; Salty cheeses, creamy cheeses.
